title: Multiple claims against an opposing party
shortTitle: Multiple claims against an opposing party
summary: Claim joinder allows a party to assert more than one claim against an existing opposing party. Federal Rule 18 provides broad procedural permission even when claims differ in subject or legal theory.
notes: Broad Rule 18 permission does not itself provide supplemental jurisdiction for an unrelated state claim. Earlier code cases such as Harris v. Avery used a narrower transaction framework.

sections.Meaning: Claim joinder allows a party to assert more than one claim against an existing opposing party. Federal Rule 18 provides broad procedural permission even when claims differ in subject or legal theory.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the existing opposing-party relationship and each proposed claim. Then test jurisdiction and other independent requirements. A court can separate matters for fair or efficient trial even though they may be pleaded together.
